messages:
maya: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector rewrite we saw a 2.3x cache-miss spike on long-sequence traffic in prod this morning. Notable P99 latency bump.
jon: ugh. do we know if it's keying or eviction behavior?
samir: I grabbed a quick profile before we rolled back: kernel pick path now annotates seq-bin + arch tag, but KV keys for persisted cache still use old key format. probably mismatch.
rachel: that would explain the misses on driver hot-swap / model bump. keys no longer match the new selectors.
profiler-bot: profiler: heap_delta=+120MB; cache_hit_rate=0.42 (was 0.78) ; p99_latency=312ms (baseline 140ms) — snapshot: https://internal/prof/3241001111
maya: copying the minimal repro log: 
```
[2026-03-18T07:12:03Z] kernel-selector: pick=arch_x86_f32_seqbin=1024->kernel=v2_opt
[2026-03-18T07:12:03Z] kv-cache: lookup key="ks:mdl:v1:seqbin:1024" -> MISS
[2026-03-18T07:12:03Z] kv-cache: lookup key="mdl:v1:seqbin:1024:prefhash" -> HIT
```
jon: so kernel-selector started prefixing arch tag into namespace but persistence writer still writes unprefixed keys. mismatch.
olga: i can push a small compat shim in the driver to check both key variants for reads for a few hours (read-path only), then log miss->alt-hit. low risk.
samir: sounds good. also want to discuss long-term: we need deterministic key schema that is stable across driver restarts but allows kernel routing variants to opt into isolation.
maya: agree. proposal: a namespaced key that separates stable model identity from routing annotations. eg: 
```
{stable_ns}:{model}@{version}::{seq_bin}::{route_tag}
```
where route_tag is optional. Read path checks both with and without route_tag. Writes include route_tag only for ephemeral cache entries.
jon: minor nit — we should avoid double-colon since some tooling expects colons only. maybe use `|` as separator?
rachel: also persistence format needs a journal with versioning so older keys are detectable for GC.
profiler-bot: quick suggestion: add a tiny metric on read-path: alt_key_hit (true/false) so we can see how many fallbacks happen.
maya: I've started a canary patch: driver will read both variants for 4 hours and emit alt_key_hit metric. will push in 2min.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered by maya: canary/kv-key-compat -> infra-canary-3 (started) :rocket:
jon: after we stabilize read compat, next step is migration: two-step rekeying job that scans and writes canonical keys for hot prefixes only. not full table rewrite.
olga: +1. we should prioritize hot prefixes by the recent access histograms. cheap rekey gives immediate benefit.
samir: for write-side: when routing changes (driver swap) we should write keys under canonical stable_ns + a low-TTL route_tag for the transient variant. that avoids poisoning persistent cache.
maya: timeline: canary read-compat now, observe alt_hit metric for 4h, then schedule hot-prefix rekey job. i'll open a runbook.
rachel: runbook should include rollback: config toggle to disable compat read and a ttl-limiter to stop writes with route_tag.
jon: question: what about model version rollouts? we need to invalidate keys when model binary changes semantics. maybe include model fingerprint hash in stable_ns.
samir: yes include model_fingerprint but at a coarse granularity (api-compat hash) to avoid churn on micro-builds.
maya: agreed. I'll draft key schema RFC and add examples + migration script. assignment: maya (author), jon (rekey job), olga (canary ops), samir (schema sign-off), rachel (runbook).
profiler-bot: scheduled: collect alt_key_hit, cache_hit_rate, p99 for next 6h.
deploy-bot: canary finished: infra-canary-3 -> success.
jon: initial metrics look promising — alt_key_hit=0.31, cache_hit_rate climbed from 0.42 -> 0.68 in first 30m.
maya: great. will post RFC link once drafted: https://go/redwood/rfc/kv-key-schema-autotune
olga: after RFC sign-off, we should add a nightly background rekey process that picks top-1k hot prefixes. cheap and incremental.
rachel: also add an invariant check in QA that ensures new selector variants cannot change stable_ns without schema bump.
samir: note for future: when we add architecture-specialized kernels, we might want per-arch ephemeral caches coalesced via a bloom filter in the stable namespace to avoid full duplication. low priority.
maya: ok wrapping up — next sync in eng-runtime tomorrow 10:30 to review RFC + rekey job plan. thanks all :thumbsup:
